title: Tools & Structured Output
objective: After this lesson you will be able to expose functions as model-callable tools with JSON schemas, validate tool arguments at the boundary, handle tool errors without breaking runs, and choose tool-calling vs direct code correctly.
why: Agents that can't act are chatbots with diagrams: order lookup, refund issuance, ticket updates all happen through tools. Tool design is API design under uncertainty — the model chooses arguments, so schemas must be strict, descriptions must disambiguate, and every result (including errors) must route somewhere sane. Most agent incidents are tool-boundary incidents.

blocks.text: A **tool** exposes a function: name, human description (the model reads this to decide *when*), and a **JSON schema** for arguments (types, enums, required, bounds). Descriptions disambiguate siblings (`lookup_order` vs `search_orders` — when each); schemas constrain choices. Undescribed tools get misused; unstrict schemas get creative arguments.

blocks.caption: Describe selection, constrain arguments, close the schema

blocks.text: Tool arguments arrive model-written: **validate against the schema at the boundary**, quarantine violations with evidence (Ch.3 nodes, same discipline), and coerce nothing silently (`'ten'` for a number is a repair-or-escalate event). Tool *results* need routing too: `{error: not-found}` flows to a clarification node, not into the draft as 'undefined'. Every tool outcome — value, empty, error — maps to an edge.

blocks.caption: Args validated, outcomes routed — tools never throw into the void

blocks.text: Let the **model** choose tools when the choice needs judgment (which of twelve tools fits this ticket?). Let **code** call functions directly when the step is deterministic (validate, compute, route on decided state — Ch.4). Model-chosen tools need descriptions + tests of selection accuracy; code-called functions need unit tests. Blurring the two (model 'deciding' a fixed step) buys flakiness at full price.

blocks.title: Guard the tool boundary
blocks.note: Run it: expect 4/4 with zero MISS — valid continues, unknown clarifies, malformed/missing quarantine. Every tool outcome lands somewhere designed; nothing throws into the void.

items: Tools = name + selection-guiding description + strict closed schema; describe siblings apart
Validate args at the boundary (quarantine with evidence); route all outcomes (value/empty/error) to edges
Model chooses tools under judgment; code calls functions under determinism — never blur the two

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice executor and confirm 4/4 routing. (b) Add an issueRefundTool (amount: number 1–500, orderId pattern) with description distinguishing it from lookup, plus three tests (valid/over-limit/malformed). (c) State which parts of a refund flow the model chooses vs code executes, with the flakiness argument.
hints: 4/4 baseline first; each outcome class (continue/clarify/quarantine) must appear in your new tests too.
issueRefund schema: {orderId pattern, amount number min 1 max 500}, required both, closed. Description: 'Issue a post-approval refund; only after approval node; lookup first for unknown orders.'
Model: which tool + free-text reason. Code: validation, limits, execution, logging. Model-decided fixed steps buy flakiness (nondeterministic correctness) at full price.
exercise.why: Tool authorship (description + schema + tests per outcome class) plus the model/code labor split are the two tool judgments — each practiced concretely, with flakiness priced honestly.
exercise.code: // Tool template: name + description (selection!) + closed schema + outcome tests.

quiz.q: lookup_order vs search_orders both exist, undescribed. Predict the failure?
options: Mis-selection: model picks arbitrarily between overlapping tools — descriptions must disambiguate siblings
quiz.explain: Tool choice follows descriptions. Undescribed siblings are a coin flip; state when-each explicitly.

quiz.q: Tool receives {amount: 'ten'} for numeric schema. Handling?
options: Quarantine with evidence (bad type + raw) for repair-or-escalate — silent coercion corrupts money flows
quiz.explain: Boundary validation with evidence, same discipline as node outputs. Money-adjacent coercion is corruption with good intentions.

quiz.q: Fixed validation step currently model-decided. Problem?
options: Flakiness at full price: deterministic steps belong in code (unit-tested); model judgment is for judgment calls
quiz.explain: Labor split by determinism: code for fixed steps, models for judgment. Blurring buys nondeterminism where correctness was achievable.

summary: Described, strict tools; validated args; routed outcomes; model/code split by judgment-vs-determinism. Tool boundaries are where agent incidents live — guard them like APIs.
next: Tooled nodes work alone — now compose graphs into teams: subgraphs, supervisors, and the patterns the CrewAI course inherits. Next: composition.
